sections.text: Enjoying solitude, abstemiousness, his body, mind and speech under perfect control, absorbed in meditation, he becomes free - always filled with the spirit of renunciation.
अहंकारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम्।
Having abandoned selfishness, power, arrogance, anger and desire, possessing nothing of his own and having attained peace, he is fit to join the Eternal Spirit.
ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति।

And when he becomes one with the Eternal, and his soul knows the bliss that belongs to the Self, he feels no desire and no regret, he regards all beings equally and enjoys the blessing of supreme devotion to Me.

So we had been discussing chapter 18, Moksa Sannyasa Yoga, Yoga of Liberation through Renunciation. So far we have seen that we are the product of our past and therefore we have tendencies, likings, and dislikings. All the discussion so far was about Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas -- this is Sattvik, this is Rajasik, and so on.
So the natural tendency is to think, Well, Ill pick the best which I can find. This looks like Sattva, so Ill just do Sattvik things only. But our tendencies and our desires and the coloring of our mind wont let us do that. So the advice from Bhagavan is Sahajam Karma kontea sadoshena PI Natya Jat.
Do the actions which come naturally to you -- those which are in line with your own personality, your tendencies, your likings, your dislikings. Do those actions even though you find them to have defects. Because I have learned 17 chapters of Bhagavad Gita now, and suddenly I find that most of my actions are Rajasik.
Thats your nature right now that comes naturally to you. Thats where the Bhagavad Gita started. Bhagavan said to Arjuna, you are a warrior.
The Rajasic action is your nature in the Kshatriya. You cant give it up right now, run towards jungle to meditate, because that will be against your tendencies in nature. That will actually create more harm to your path of evolution than help you.
It wont purify your mind, pollute your mind and confuse your mind. So Sahajam Karma kaun teja sadoshana pen Natya Jat. Do not give up the actions which come naturally to you.
Even though you find some defects, they are not perfect. And then Bhagavan said that by doing so you will purify yourself and consolation given to Sarvarambahi kadushena dumena agnihi ava vritaha all actions, no matter how pure you see them have some defects. There is always a side effect to even the best medicine you can take.
The Bhagavan said Any actions which you have to perform in accordance with your nature even if you find the faults in it, continue. Because every action will have its own defects. But then what do I do with it? The only thing you can do is perfect your attitude towards your actions.
Actions by nature has their own pluses and minuses but you can change your attitude towards your actions. So the next few verses which we have seen say Asakta Buddhi -- the first thing you do is detach your intellect from your actions. Asaktabuddhi Sarvatra Jitatma Vigataspruhaha -- Im doing these things because they come naturally to me.
As I said, Gita class is a Kamya Karma for me, because I like to do it, it is my desire to do it. So if it comes naturally to you, do it. But Bhagavan said, Asaktabuddhehe -- detach your mind and intellect from those actions.
Sarvatra Jitatma -- have self-control over your desires, your likings, and dislikes. Im doing it, but I may not have any control of the outcome. I may not be allowed to do these things; the environment, the situation may not allow me.
I need to be content with that, without attachment. I want to do it, but if there is no opportunity to do it, Ill continue with what is available to me. The goal here is to achieve a state of Naishkarmya Siddhi -- whatever I do, I do not feel that Im doing it.
As I said, when we are working on our hobbies, its not work. Im putting in lots of effort, but I dont consider it work because thats my hobby. The other day Krishna told me, Im going to call you.
Were going to practice together. Because when we are not practicing, its not really working. When are you going to call me? Well, Saturday Im not available, because that becomes work for me. Naishkarmya Siddhi is like this: when everything I do becomes my hobby, I become actionless. Its all basically in line with my nature.
Paramam Sanyasena Adhigacchati -- such a person achieves the highest level of renunciation. By doing the things which you are supposed to do, you can achieve sannyasa. The definition of sannyasa is giving up the sense of agency.
Not giving up things and beings, but giving up the sense of agency -- I am doing it and I am enjoying it. When you give that up, you are a sannyasi. Bhagavan said, if you do all the things in line with your nature, you will never have that sense of agency, nor will you even notice that you are enjoying it. You get so engrossed in the stuff which you do for your hobby that neither you are aware that you are putting lots of efforts into it, nor whether its painful or enjoyable.
Music practice was the most painful thing I had when I was going to my teachers classes for that little time. But it was still what I wanted to do. So whether it was a pain or a joy, I never noticed it.
This is something I want to do. That Bhagavan says -- in that state you are neither aware that you are the doer nor aware that you are the enjoyer. When you achieve that state, you have achieved sannyasa.
With that the next verse says Siddhim prapto yatha brahma tatha apnoti nibodame sama se nay kaunteya nista gnana seya yapara. Now Ill tell you in brief how to reach Brahman, having achieved that siddhi -- the Naishkarmya Siddhi. Now everything comes naturally to me.
I do everything naturally. I dont have any anxiety about whether Im enjoying or suffering through it, or whether good will come out of it. I just enjoy doing it.
Therefore Im doing it. He said, achieving that siddhi in your actions and achieving sannyasa through that -- how you can then achieve Brahman, I will tell you now. So now comes the prescription or the detailed guidance of how to achieve that.
The verse we have seen after that is Buddaya visuddaya Yuktah dhruti atmanam niyam yucha. First thing is Buddaya Vishuddaya -- you have to purify your intellect. My intellect is right now polluted by my ego.
My ego says I am always right, even though everybody else says otherwise. My intellect says I am the smartest among all. So Buddhaya Vishuddaya -- the purified intellect will see things as they are.
The intellect is purified by not having ego polluting it. Dhruti Atmanam -- be firm in your own self. This is what I want to do.
This is what I like to do. And this is where I am putting my efforts. Dhruti Atmanam firm in your own self.
What is my true nature? I know what I really like. I was just listening to NPR yesterday and some guy who was a lawyer and has a nice corporate practice, he gives up and becomes a LEGO artist. I dont know whether anybody heard that.
In other words, he makes complex form of lions and stuff. Hes basically an artist whose work is now displayed all these places. But he gave up the job and became a LEGO artist.
And LEGO company provides him free logos. When they have a new LEGO comes out in thousands and he creates whatever. He said that the worst day as an artist is better than the best day as a lawyer.
For me, therefore I did it. He found what he likes. He followed Bhagavad Gita without reading it.
I want to do this no matter what the outcome may be. But this is what I like. Buddaya Visuddhaya Having purified my intellect, what is my true nature? Our intellect typically gets polluted by worrying about what others will think of us.
And therefore we make choices accordingly. We choose our profession -- at least in my time it was very simple. You didnt have to figure out what you like.
If you dont get admission in medicine, go to chemical engineering. Chemical engineering doesnt work out? Go to mechanical engineering. Mechanical doesnt work out? Electrical.
Then civil. And if you are completely out of all that, go to architecture. You didnt have to figure out what you like.
You just figured out what the social scale was. Bhagavan said thats a perfect recipe for disaster for you. Dhruti Atmanam Niyamyacha Sabdayati Visayam Tektva Ragadveso, vidashyacha sabdadi sound, etc.
In other words, all the sense objects from outside which is polluting your mind and intellect. You are not getting disturbed by this. I wish I can become an artist but there is no money in it.
Doctors make more money, so let me go to medicine even though I hate that profession. There was one guy on Kaun Banega Karorpati. He had just done his internship, and Amitabh Bachchan asked him, So after that, what next? He said, What do you mean? Dont you want to do MD or MS or something? He said, Yeah, I can do MD or MS, but Im not interested in it. Why are you not interested in furthering your career? He said, I dont like medicine.
My parents wanted me to go to medicine. Thats why I went to medicine. But I want to be an IAS officer. Ive seen IAS officers.
Ive seen what they do and their power and their influence. And thats what I want to be. So I did what my parents wanted me to do.
Now Im going to do what I want to do. And how do I achieve this purified intellect and self-control? Vivikta Sevi, Laghvashi -- now comes the discipline or guidance for how you can find out what you really like. How do you find out what your true nature is? How do I align my actions with my own nature? Vivikta Sevi -- solitude.
Solitude is something we think about. We are all afraid of loneliness. Ill tell you -- when we were young, if on Saturday you had no invitation to go to any party, we didnt know what to do. Rajan, what are you doing over the weekend? So Rajan, how was your weekend? I said, Its always the same.
My weekends are always the same. Which party did you go to? If you dont get invited to a party, you dont know what to do with your life. That weekend youre completely lost. Learn to be happy with yourself.
Find a way that you can enjoy solitude. That you think, thank God nobody is now here. I can be by myself and enjoy my time.
Im sure most of your parents went through that. But solitude is a practice to figure out how you can enjoy yourself by yourself. Laghvashi -- eating but little.
Other texts say: eat as much as you would take your medicine. Your medication -- you never take more than what your doctor says you should take. One tablet means one tablet.
Thats what the doctor said, right? Not, Well, the doctor says one, but Im a little more aggressive about it, so Im going to take three at a time. Take only what you need. Your food should be just like that -- only what you need. The texts elaborately describe that a quarter of your belly should be filled with food, a quarter left for water, and half left for air.
That much you should eat -- Laghvashi -- because you know that when youre overstuffed, youre uncomfortable and the mind is not available for anything else. Laghvashi Yata-Vak-Kaya-Manasaha -- control over your speech, body, and mind. Vak (speech) includes all organs of action.
Its an indicator: all the organs of action should be in control. It does not say stop them -- just keep them in control through moderation. Kaya -- body.
The body is the gross form of my mind.

These verses provide the complete prescription for Self-realization. Verse 52 lists the practices: vivikta-sevi (cultivating solitude), laghvashi (eating lightly), yata-vak-kaya-manasa (controlling speech, body, and mind), dhyana-yoga-para (devoted to meditation), and vairagyam samupashrita (established in dispassion). These are not random austerities but a coherent program for purifying the instrument through which we perceive reality. Notice the emphasis on moderation - laghu (light) eating, yata (controlled) faculties - not extreme suppression.
Verse 53 lists what must be abandoned: ahamkara (ego), bala (force/power), darpa (arrogance), kama (desire), krodha (anger), and parigraha (possessiveness). Casting these off, one becomes nirmama (without mine-ness) and shanta (peaceful), qualifying for Brahma-bhuyaya - becoming one with Brahman. Verse 54 describes the result: Brahma-bhuta (established in Brahman), prasannatma (serene-minded), neither grieving nor craving, equal toward all beings, and attaining supreme devotion.
The path is clear but challenging. Today, practice vivikta-seva - cultivating moments of solitude, even briefly. Examine your laghu-ashi - are you eating more than needed? Practice yata-vak - restraint in speech before responding. These small adjustments accumulate. Also examine: where does ahamkara (ego) drive your actions? Where does parigraha (possessiveness) create suffering? Identify one instance of each today and consciously release it. The promise is profound: through consistent practice, one attains prasannatma - a naturally serene mind that neither grieves loss nor craves gain.
